# Laboratory Techniques and Safety

## Core ideas and reasoning

Laboratory work requires identifying hazards and choosing controls before starting. Wear suitable eye protection, secure loose hair, keep containers labelled and never taste chemicals or pipette by mouth. Read a liquid meniscus at eye level to reduce parallax; for a clear aqueous solution use the bottom of the meniscus. A burette volume delivered is final reading minus initial reading, not the final reading alone. Rinse apparatus appropriately to avoid dilution or contamination: a burette with the solution it will deliver and a pipette with the solution it will measure. A conical titration flask may be rinsed with distilled water because extra water does not change the moles already pipetted into it. Record measurements with units and appropriate precision and repeat readings to identify consistency. Heat a test tube gently with its opening pointed away from people, and use a holder. Deal with spills under laboratory supervision. Never supply missing experimental readings or infer an unshown apparatus label.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Explain parallax error when reading a measuring cylinder.

If the eye is above or below the meniscus, its apparent level shifts relative to the scale. Read at eye level to reduce this error.

### Example 2

A burette reads 2.30 cm³ initially and 24.85 cm³ finally. Find the volume delivered.

24.85 - 2.30 = 22.55 cm³. The initial liquid already below the zero mark must be accounted for.

### Example 3

Why must a pipette not be filled by mouth?

Chemicals could enter the mouth or be inhaled. Use a suitable pipette filler to reduce exposure.

### Example 4

Why is a Bunsen burner set to a luminous flame when it is not being used for heating?

The luminous flame is clearly visible, making an unattended flame easier to notice and reducing accidental contact.

### Example 5

Give two reasons why a luminous Bunsen flame is unsuitable for heating.

It is smoky or sooty and is less hot than the non-luminous heating flame. Soot contaminates apparatus.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
